text:
alex: thinking out loud — we should add a per-route "permission chooser" when creating routes in Console so teams can pick role/entitlement combos instead of the current global role dropdown

maya: +1, the global dropdown causes too many support tickets. can we show scoped presets like 'read-only metrics', 'invoke-only', 'manage-rollouts' ? :thinking_face:

cheng: agree. also need to clarify how quotas map to roles — e.g., a token with 'invoke-only' can still exhaust project quota unless we tie token->quota rules

sophia: quick sketch idea: when you add a route you pick: 1) role preset 2) scope (project/org/resource) 3) optional quota override. UI shows a short permission summary and an audit link.

alex: love that. security question: do we allow overlapping scopes where a user might have broader org role but restricted route role? which wins?

security-bot: SECURITY: policy precedence must be deterministic. Proposed default: explicit route scope overrides inherited role for that route only. Inheritance still applies elsewhere. Audit log must record overrides.

maya: ok route overrides win, but we should display a callout: "This route has an explicit override — users with broader access may still bypass unless role denied at org level" (cc @security-bot)

cheng: implementation note: backend will need a fast evaluation order: 1) explicit route rules 2) project-level role 3) org-level role 4) deny-list. Keep as short-circuit checks — don't do heavy evals on hot path.

alex: UX question: where to surface telemetry links? we want per-route cost & latency dashboard but only for people with 'metrics-view' entitlement. If someone lacks it, show greyed-out card with request to request access.

sophia: yes, show card with icons and 'request access' button that opens entitlement request flow (pre-filled). Should tie to just-in-time access approval.

maya: entitlement requests should auto-fill manager and justification fields. devex can wire that to the approval API.

cheng: edge case: enterprise customers with SCIM/AD sync — we need to map external groups to these presets. Suggest we add a "group-mapping" admin table in Private/Dedicated.

alex: +1. Also for Dedicated customers we might expose a JSON policy editor (advanced mode) that lets them write route-level policies. Show both UI and raw JSON toggle.

sophia: example policy block (for devs):
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/summarize",
  "role": "invoke-only",
  "scope": "project:internal-ux",
  "quota": {"per_minute": 60},
  "audit": "override"
}
```

maya: love the raw view. we must validate schema client-side and prevent escalation via malformed scopes.

security-bot: REMINDER: all policy changes must be stored in the audit index and emitted as events for SIEM. Also ensure KMS-wrapped tokens not logged.

alex: next steps: sophia to prototype a chooser component + request access flow mock, cheng to spec evaluation algorithm and performance constraints, maya to define product presets & entitlement names. I'll follow up with a short RFC by EOD Tuesday.

cheng: I'll stub a simple algorithm doc and put perf numbers we want (<=100us check on hot path).

sophia: I'll drop Figma link when ready.

maya: noted — I'll assemble preset matrix and enterprise mapping notes.

alex: thanks all. tagging for follow-up: @sophia @cheng @maya. :rocket:
